1.name: Crankcase
1.note: The die-cast housing that carries the crankshaft and bolts the cylinder on top. Everything the piston pushes on is reacted through it.

2.name: Flywheel web, counterweighted
2.note: The crank webs. Their counterweights balance the piston, and their inertia carries the crank through the three strokes that do no work.

3.name: Crankpin
3.note: Joins the two webs and offsets the rod from the axis. This offset is what turns the piston's straight push into rotation.

4.name: Needle cage
4.note: A roller bearing between crankpin and rod big end. It lets the rod swing round the pin with very little friction.

5.name: Connecting rod
5.note: Links piston to crankpin. It carries the gas force down as a push and turns the piston's up-and-down motion into the crank's circle.

6.name: Gudgeon pin
6.note: A hollow pin joining the small end of the rod to the piston, so the rod can tilt as the crank turns.

7.name: Piston
7.note: Takes the gas pressure on its crown. Its upward travel compresses the charge and its downward travel is the power stroke.

8.name: Top ring
8.note: The main gas seal. It keeps the compression and combustion pressure above the piston and out of the crankcase.

9.name: Second ring
9.note: A back-up gas seal that also scrapes oil down on the down-stroke.

10.name: Oil ring
10.note: Wipes surplus oil off the liner, so it does not burn in the chamber.

11.name: Cylinder liner
11.note: The hard iron bore the piston and rings slide in. It sets the bore that, with the stroke, gives the swept volume.

12.name: Cylinder barrel, finned
12.note: Holds the liner and carries combustion heat out through its fins to the passing air.

13.name: Head gasket
13.note: A multi-layer steel seal between barrel and head. It holds the peak cylinder pressure in the chamber.

14.name: Cylinder head, finned
14.note: Closes the top of the cylinder and forms the combustion chamber. It carries the valves, the plug and both camshafts.

15.name: Valve seat insert
15.note: A hard ring pressed into the head. The valve face closes on it to seal the port.

16.name: Valve guide
16.note: A bushing that keeps each valve stem on its axis, so the valve lands squarely on its seat.

17.name: Inlet valve
17.note: Opens to let the fresh charge in on the intake stroke and stays shut for compression and the power stroke.

18.name: Exhaust valve
18.note: Opens to let burned gas out on the exhaust stroke. It is smaller than the inlet and made of a more heat-resistant steel.

19.name: Valve stem seal
19.note: Wipes the stem so oil from the cam cover does not run down the guide into the port.

20.name: Valve spring
20.note: Shuts the valve and keeps the tappet following the cam. The cam only opens the valve; the spring closes it.

21.name: Spring retainer
21.note: A cap on the stem end that the spring pushes against.

22.name: Valve collet
22.note: Two split cones that lock the retainer to a groove in the valve stem.

23.name: Bucket tappet + shim
23.note: The cam pushes on this cup, which presses the valve open. The shim under it sets the valve clearance.

24.name: Inlet camshaft
24.note: Its lobe sets how far and when the inlet valve lifts. It turns at half crank speed, so each valve opens once per two crank turns.

25.name: Exhaust camshaft
25.note: Same job for the exhaust valve, with its lobe timed to open before the piston reaches the bottom of the power stroke.

26.name: Cam cover
26.note: Closes the top of the head and keeps oil in around the cams and tappets.

27.name: Spark plug
27.note: Fires a spark in the chamber before top dead centre. The flame grows from its tip across the charge and starts the power stroke.

28.name: Inlet manifold
28.note: Carries the fresh charge from the throttle to the inlet port.

29.name: Exhaust pipe
29.note: Carries burned gas away from the exhaust port.
